correctness.rationale: Adding the predator equation to the prey equation after multiplying the latter by the assimilation coefficient cancels predation and yields a quadratic with exactly one positive predator root. Substitution into the prey equilibrium equation gives the attack-rate branch. Its limit at zero prey is exactly the predator-only invasion threshold. The small-prey expansion has a positive first correction and the Jacobian determinant has the corresponding negative leading term, so the nearby coexistence equilibrium is a saddle. Fresh numerical reconstruction at the source parameters gives threshold 0.208, coexistence equilibria near (8.3358197853,54.8152125587) and (32.0797287675,54.6492858751) at attack rate 0.8, with determinants approximately −0.04513 and 0.06983 respectively; the small branch expansion tends to the predicted unit coefficient.

final_claim: In the Acotto–Venturino herd-response predator-prey model, every positive coexistence equilibrium is parameterized by prey density through the stated positive predator branch and attack-rate function; the only predator-only boundary collision occurs at the exact prey-invasion threshold, and the local coexistence branch on the higher-attack side is a saddle, so the source's reported larger numerical transcritical value is not that boundary collision.
